answer: Each identity mounts one timber fender pile on a jetty, locks an 85-credit bond, and keys its serial to its key. Each epoch a boat sends a ripple against the jetty; the identity logs crest height and its compression. An auditor recomputes compression from the timber ripple-load table by crest height, diameter and species. Over 3 percent off, reused serial, or copied log burns the bond. First pays 42, the k-th 42+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 3,039,000 plus 85,000 locked, each needing its own pile. A rented-fender ring fails: borrowed readings carry a foreign serial. An honest agent pays 42 once.
